findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment:
Observed the following instances of improper storage:
(i) 1ST REPEAT: Soup/Salad bowls were stored on open shelves near the prep line upright instead of inverted, and are open to falling debris through the upper shelves. PIC was notified and plans to place mats on the upper shelves to protect the dishes and prevent falling debris, as the shape of the bowls does not allow for inversion.
(ii) Clean bowls and other dishes were stored in the dish room in the open and upright position instead of protected or inverted. Of particular concern were large metal bowls that were air-drying where the water inside was not able to drain because they were not inverted. CORRECTED: the bowls were inverted during the inspection, and PIC was notified that all clean articles need to be protected by inversion or a cover.
Ensure all equipment, utensils, and single-service or single-use articles are kept protected through cover or inversion.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed several items that were being stored past their date-marked discard date. PIC voluntarily disposed of the items. It is important that items not only are properly date-marked with the day of prep being day 1 and day 7 being the date where the item must be used or discarded, but that out-of-date items are then discarded per the written date-mark.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following instances of improper storage:
1) bowls were stored on open shelves upright instead of inverted and were open to falling debris through the shelves;
2) utensils were stored upright instead of inverted in the drying racks.
The PIC was notified of all instances.
1) The shape of the bowls is not conducive to inversion, so the PIC plans to place mats on the above shelves to protect the dishes and prevent falling debris.
2) The utensils were removed and washed and replaced in an inverted position.
It is important that all equipment, utensils, and single-service or single-use articles are kept protected through cover or inversion.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed a build-up of debris in the following locations:
1) (1ST REPEAT) The debris on the floor of the outside shed that stores single-use articles.
2) The debris surrounding the microwave in the front kitchen area.
3) The splashes and debris in the bottom of both milk coolers.
4) The debris surrounding the bread slicer.
The PIC was notified and planned to add it to the cleaning schedule.
It is important that food-contact and non-food contact surfaces are kept free of accumulated dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of black mold and deterioration of caulking near the dish machine and triple sink. PIC was notified and made plans for cleaning and re-caulking. It is important that all physical facilities be maintained and in good repair, and that equipment that cannot be moved is kept sealed to prevent the building of moisture and debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces: 

(1) The caulking on the back of house coffee table is disconnected on the right side causing a gap between the wall and table. The table must be properly caulked because it cannot be removed from the wall for cleaning. The caulking on the right side must be replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface.

(2) There are several small holes in the wall within the dish washing room. The holes are from shelving that was removed. The holes must be filled (ex.caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface.

Ensure that the above referenced are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned: 

(1) The accumulation of soil debris behind the soda nozzles on the drive through and customer drink dispensers. 

(2) The dust on the shelves holding clean dishes and equipment above the non-functioning prep coolers in the dish washing room. 

(3) The debris on the floor of the outside shed that stores single-use articles. 

Ensure that the above referenced non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
A rack above clean utensils was observed to have an accumulation of dust and food debris. Discussed with PIC the potentials of cross contamination. Ensure that cleaned and sanitized utensils are always stored in a manner that prevents them from contamination. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S)

During the previous inspection, several of the front edges of the shelving underneath the register counter have begun to peel. Underneath the peeling trim is exposed wood which is not smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. During the inspection today, inspector observed that these shelves remain out-of-compliance. Ensure that these surfaces are made smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The hand sink along the east wall of the kitchen near the register and bread pans did not have any paper towels in the dispenser or nearby. All hand sinks must be stocked with paper towels at all times to facilitate hand washing. Ensure that hand sinks are stocked with paper towels and soap at all times. Operator immediately added paper towels to the dispenser. Corrected on site. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine sanitizing stage did not register any chlorine concentration on SCDPH test strips or facility test strips. Operator made multiple attempts to correct the problem including priming but was unable to get the dish machine functioning within required limits. As such, facility has been instructed to cease use of the dish machine for sanitizing operations. Machine may be used for cleaning but all items washed through the dish machine or sink must be sanitized in the third (sanitizing) basin of the triple sink prior to use/storage. Operator states that the dish machine concentration is tested on a daily basis. Operator has been instructed to call SCDPH inspector when repairs have been made by EcoLab and prior to using the dish machine for sanitizing operations. If no corrections have been made prior, inspector will return on 01/06/2023 to evaluate progress of repairs and ensure that facility continues to utilize the triple sink for ALL sanitizing operations. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Inspector observed individually packaged containers of sliced meat stored in a broken box on the floor of the walk-in freezer underneath shelving. Foods must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. Foods may not be stored under sources of contamination (i.e. underneath shelving units). Ensure that foods are protected from contamination by storing in a dry, clean location at least 6 inches above the ground at all times. Operator immediately removed food from this location and discarded it. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Baking sheets throughout the facility which are used for baking bread in-house are observed to be soiled/worn to the point that cleaning of the sheets is no longer possible. Baking sheets are brown to black in color due to long-term use and are visible soiled with accumulated burnt residue and debris. The accumulation of residue on these baking sheets creates a surface which can no longer be cleaned easily.  Baking sheets must be cleaned or resurfaced to be free of residue or replaced by the next routine inspection which will occur in mid-2023. Per conversation with person-in-charge, facility has been trying to power wash these pans to remove residue and debris. Inspector observed that pans which were power still had residue and debris present and had scoring as a result of use and the power washing process.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The right-hand cabinet underneath the lemonade counter in the dining area is observed to have a significant amount of spilled lemonade accumulating on both top and bottom shelf of the cabinet. This cabinet must be cleaned. Ensure that non-food-contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent accumulation of residue and debris and that spills are cleaned up at the time they occur. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the broom/dustpan combination were stored immediately leaning on pans which held packaged containers of bread and other items. Brooms, mops and other maintenance items must be stored in a location which does not pose the risk of the contaminating food. Ensure that maintenance tools are stored properly between uses. Inspector moved the broom so that it no longer touched packages of food during the inspection and discussed with person-in-charge. Corrected on site. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas of the floor along the base coving tile in the walk-in freezer are observed to have a significant amount of residue and debris accumulating. Clean underneath these shelves by the next routine inspection. Ensure that the areas underneath shelving and equipment are cleaned on a regular basis to prevent the accumulation of soil throughout the facility.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

Ensure that all surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable and those subject to food and moisture are non-absorbent prior to the next routine inspection.

(B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Upon inspection of the facility, inspector observed three problem areas which had been pointed out to PIC during the complaint inspection on 9/14/2022 that have not been cleaned to prevent pests in the facility. These areas include:
- Under the soda machine where there is visibly soiled countertop and trash buildup.
- Under the counter in the bread prep area where the soil built up against the walls is very thick; observed debris, residues and a heavily soiled probe thermometer.
- Under the counters across from the drive-thru area where the ground and walls is soiled.

Some improvement had been made. Inspector had been told by PIC during prior inspection that these areas were being actively cleaned throughout the course of the inspection. However, the cleaning is not sufficient to preclude the accumulation of debris nor is it sufficient enough to reduce/eliminate the occurrence of pests. Inspector observed that cleaning was very superficial as there is still soup residue under the counter in the drive thru which had soup on it. The wall had been wiped, but not even enough to remove the obvious soup at the base of the wall. Under the soda machine had been obviously wiped, but only in the most obvious of areas, leaving the most soiled areas unclean. 

There was no sign of live ants during the follow-up today. Flies were still present in the facility today, however, their numbers were significantly reduced. Dead ants were observed in the areas mentioned previously as being soiled, especially by the soda machine on the wall under the drive thru window.

A second follow-up is being issued for 10 days from today on 10/03/2022. Continue cleaning efforts and ensure that employees understand cleaning must be a DEEP cleaning to get the debris and residue which are not being cleaned on a regular basis. PIC is aware of the areas that must be cleaned and has stated that she sees the soiled areas that must be clean before return inspection. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Person in charge is a CFM. However, during complaint follow-up today, inspector observed that the PIC had priority foundation violations. Person in charge was also unsure of pest control in the facility when asked. The person in charge is responsible for ensuring that harborage conditions in the facility are prevented and that pest control is contacted as necessary which has not been occurring. Inspector will return in 30 days to determine if the facility has improved cleaning practices, removed harborage conditions, begun or scheduled maintenance/repairs, and eliminated insects from the facility. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed ants and flies throughout the facility. Flies appeared to congregate at the front of the store and ants appeared to be more present at the back of the store. There was no obvious nesting area for either pest. Inspector observed all corners and underneath equipment throughout the facility. Ants were present diffusely throughout the facility although not in great numbers at this time. Flies were also present diffusely but again, not in great numbers. Call Pesto-X and have them visit the facility to eliminate ants and flies. 

Several areas throughout the facility are harborage areas for pests. Underneath equipment, there is refuse that has been dropped and not cleaned up including single use items like cups and lids and other food debris. The drive thru in particular had a significant amount of residue under the soda machine. Behind the soup hot holding at the drive thru, inspector observed soup which had been allowed to drip down the wall, puddle on the floor and dry. The dish room is in need of in-depth cleaning in all corners of the room as there is a significant amount of residue, debris and refuse in corners and underneath cabinets. 

These conditions all contribute to the pest problem in the facility. Ensure that they care corrected before the follow-up on 9/23/2022. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Non-food contact surfaces, especially the bottom of equipment and shelving underneath equipment and materials is observed to be soiled at the time of inspection. Although the facility is busy, much of the residue found underneath equipment and materials is much older than todays debris based on total accumulation and the condition/dryness of the debris/residue. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned frequently enough to preclude the accumulation of debris and other substances. Regular cleaning of these areas will help prevent pests such as ants and flies from becoming prevalent in the facility. Ensure that these areas are cleaned regularly.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the dish room has many tiles which are damaged and/or peeling away from the floor/wall. Tiles at the wall-floor junction behind the dish machine and sink are observed to be peeling from the wall all the way across the back wall. The sink/dish machine is also not appropriate caulked. Thus, water is able to drip behind the sink and down behind the tiles at the base wall. Tiles to the right of the sink in the dish room are observed to be cracked at the base of the tile directly at the junction of the floor and wall. This crack is large and progresses from one corner to the other. These tiles need repaired/replaced. There are also tiles to the left of the dish machine which are peeling back from the wall and need replaced. Inspector also observed two tiles under and to the left of the dish machine on the floor which have shattered. All of these areas contribute to pest harborage conditions in the facility. These need to be replaced. Ensure that caulking and tile repairs/replacements are completed prior to the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Observed employee removing her gloves and placing new gloves on without washing hands in between during food preparation on the front line. Same employee was observed washing hands after removing gloves again but did not lather for 20 seconds after applying soap before rinsing the soap off her hands. All employees need to follow proper hand washing procedures including washing between glove changes and lathering hands with soap for at least 20 seconds. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all employees are aware of proper hand washing protocol. COS.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

Sani buckets in the facility are not showing appreciable levels of lactic acid sanitizer on either the inspector’s, nor the facility’s, tests strips. Checking the two machines in the facility show that neither is properly dispensing solution for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Inspector walked the PIC through manually making the solution from the jug.  Buckets were manually made during the inspection to correct the violation and will continue to be made manually until service can be conducted by EcoLab. PIC stated they would call in the morning for service. Inspector will spot check later in the week to ensure that service is completed.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

Sanitizer buckets are observed at approximately 100 ppm quat on the inspector's test strips. Investigation showed that the solution coming out of the machine appears to have a low concentration coming out of it. PIC called Ecolab to see when maintenance/adjustment could be completed. At the time the inspection ended they had not contacted the PIC. Follow-up in 3 days.

findings.comment: Observed quat sanitation bucket to be at 0ppm. Ensure sanitizer is checked routinely and replaced when falls below label requirements. Corrected. PIC added quat sanitizer to buckets. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed black residue starting to develop on ice machine. In addition ovens have soil accumulation. Ensure equipment is cleaned as needed to prevent accumulation. Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed pipe connected to condenser in walk-in fridge (near personal item area) accumulating ice build-up. Ice from the pipe has the potential to cross-contaminate by falling onto food. Ensure all food is protected from any contamination. Routine maintenance of cooling units should be conducted to prevent further failures. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed utensil used for obtaining tree nut to be inside of food container. Food dispensing utensils must be properly stored in food. 
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed black debris found on ice machine. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as needed.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service knifes to be laid in no particular manner. All single service utensils must be dispensed in manner to prevent contamination. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed clean knives stored in between equipment. This is not a proper practice. Store clean utensils to protect them from potential contamination.
